Plot Principal Component Analysis of Yield Curve Movements

Source: R/dns-visualization.r
plot_yield_pca.Rd

Performs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on yield curve movements and visualizes the results.

Usage

plot_yield_pca(
  yield_data,
  n_components = 3,
  plot_weights = TRUE,
  plot_scores = TRUE,
  plot_variance = TRUE,
  scale = TRUE
)

Arguments

yield_data

Data frame. Historical yield curve data with 'Date' column.

n_components

Integer. Number of principal components to extract.

plot_weights

Logical. If TRUE, plot the loadings (eigenvectors).

plot_scores

Logical. If TRUE, plot the scores (projections).

plot_variance

Logical. If TRUE, plot the explained variance.

scale

Logical. Whether to standardise each maturity's change series before the decomposition. TRUE is the default, preserving earlier behaviour. FALSE decomposes the covariance matrix instead, which is the usual convention for yield curves: it lets the more volatile maturities carry more weight, and is what gives the familiar level, slope and curvature shapes.

Value

A list containing:

  • pca: The PCA result object

  • plots: A list of created plots

Examples

data(treasury_yields)

# scale = FALSE decomposes the covariance matrix, the usual convention for
# yield curves, which is what produces the level/slope/curvature shapes
pca_result <- plot_yield_pca(treasury_yields, scale = FALSE)
round(pca_result$var_explained[1:3], 4)
#> [1] 0.7160 0.1087 0.0991
pca_result$plots$weights
